title: The French farm is assigned to strengthen Kirtland as a stake
setting: High priests met on 4 June 1833 in the translating room of Newel K. Whitney’s store in Kirtland, Ohio. The church had recently bought the 103-acre farm of Peter French. The council could not agree on who should manage it, so they agreed to ask the Lord. Joseph Smith dictated this revelation during the meeting. That same day, the council put Whitney in charge of the farm and admitted John Johnson to the United Firm.
summary: The revelation says this stake, set “for the strength of Zion,” must be made strong. Newel K. Whitney is to take charge of the place where the Lord’s house will be built. The land is to be divided into lots for those seeking inheritances, as the council decides. A portion is to serve the order’s purpose of bringing forth the Lord’s word. The voice calls the spread of that word “most expedient,” to subdue people’s hearts. John Johnson’s offering is accepted, and he is promised eternal life if he keeps the commandments. He is called a descendant of Joseph and is to join the order. He is to remove the debts on “the house named among you” so that he may live there.

contextNote.title: Land managed so the word can go out
contextNote.text: The council disagreed over a piece of land, and the answer turned to its purpose. Verse 2 gives Whitney charge of the place chosen for the Lord’s house. Verse 4 reserves part of the land for the order’s work of “bringing forth my word”. Verse 5 calls this work “the most expedient,” so that hearts may be subdued. Verse 8 gives the same reason for adding John Johnson to the order. In this passage, expedient means the most needed use, the one that serves the spread of the Lord’s word.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 94–97, “For the Salvation of Zion,” treats Kirtland’s growth as part of building Zion. How do verses 1 and 5 tie a practical decision about land to the spread of the Lord’s word?
reviewNote: Read all 9 verses. Official heading gives 4 June 1833, a conference of high priests unable to agree on managing the French farm near Kirtland. JSP introduction read for the meeting in Whitney’s store, the 103-acre purchase, and same-day actions on Whitney and John Johnson. “Incumbrances” in verse 9 is rendered as debts; the JSP introduction does not specify them, and which house is meant is not stated. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes. Setting checked against the official heading and JSP historical introduction.
